insight: Swarm responsive TUI rows must bound compactElapsed for migrated schema-v0 sessions whose LastActivity is zero: time.Since(time.Time{}) renders 106751d and overflows the six-cell elapsed field. Cap day output at 9999d so the token retains its unit plus one separator cell, and include zero LastActivity in width tests.

For Swarm's Working indicator, the selected design is the full one-cell Braille orbit ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, advanced by the existing one-second general-view repaint. Keep the HTML preview's selected card, implementation frames, wraparound test, golden fixture, and ANSI style pins synchronized.

Swarm's ten-frame Braille Working loop feels glitchy at the inherited 1000 ms/frame repaint (a 10-second full loop). Before changing production cadence, compare synchronized 60, 80, 100, 125, 160, and 220 ms/frame variants; use 80 ms/frame as the starting recommendation and include 1000 ms as the control.

Swarm smooth Braille animation should use a dedicated 90 ms view-scoped tick separate from the one-second elapsed repaint. The glyph tick must avoid ClearScreen, keep at most one in-flight timer, and run only on the general board while at least one row is Working.

On tf-wks-nathan, Swarm TUI performance tests that start a real daemon must run outside the managed sandbox: Unix-socket setsockopt is denied inside it. A sandbox failure at skeleton.Serve listen unix is environmental; rerun the exact test outside before diagnosing source.

On tf-wks-nathan the installed GitHub CLI predates gh auth token; that command emits usage text and makes GoReleaser reject the Authorization header. For Swarm publishing, pass GITHUB_TOKEN from gh config get oauth_token --host github.com without printing it, then install both released binaries and restart the daemon while checking the live-session roster.

Swarm handoff must be a first-class CLI-and-prompt framework, not a skill, plugin, MCP server, or slash-command installation. The TUI should inject a complete vendor-neutral prompt that tells the source agent to author context, invoke the built-in swarm handoff CLI, and supervise with watch/peek/send.

A first-class swarm handoff must resolve its live source from SWARM_SESSION_ID plus the daemon roster, inherit the roster cwd, copy context under Swarm state, preserve SpawnedFrom/SpawnIntent=handoff, and reserve stdout for the child session id alone so supervision commands can consume it.

For supervised handoff, swarm watch accepts a comma-separated set of attention states so one event-driven subscription can wake on needs_input, ready_for_review, or completed. Keep change exclusive because it intentionally ignores the initial snapshot and matches every later event.

For Swarm TUI handoff, never gate on the derived needs_input group because it combines ordinary prompts with permission requests. Gate raw process/turn/interaction, capture the source ID, revalidate at submit, and render the complete CLI-only supervision prompt below protocol.MaxSendInputText before SendInput with Submit true.

On tf-wks-nathan, run Swarm's golangci-lint with GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE under /tmp because the default runtime cache is read-only in the managed workspace. For subcommand usage constants, assign FlagSet.Usage so the contract is both user-visible on --help and not dead code.

For Swarm release dry-runs on tf-wks-nathan, use the repo-pinned prebuilt GoReleaser 2.17.0, put the cached go1.25.0 toolchain bin first on PATH with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, and set TMPDIR plus GOCACHE under /tmp. The host /usr/local/go binary says 1.25.0 but its GOROOT VERSION is 1.24.1, and the managed runtime temp path is read-only.

Use a Codex skill under ~/.agents/skills and invoke it through /skills or , or inject a vendor-neutral prompt.

A single local integration directory can be validated and installed by both current Codex and Claude Code when it contains parallel .codex-plugin/plugin.json and .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifests, one shared skills/<name>/SKILL.md, and one shared .mcp.json. Each CLI still needs its own marketplace manifest and explicit install command; Codex policy.installation=INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT only made the local plugin available in the isolated validation and did not install it.

Swarm TUI handoff injection must not treat every needs_input row as a safe composer. status.GroupNeedsInput includes InteractionPermission, so submitting a natural-language handoff there can answer or corrupt a permission dialog. Gate on the raw status: allow ready_for_review and explicit prompt interactions, refuse permission, working, and completed; re-check at form submission.

For Swarm handoff, the user requires a CLI-first architecture, not MCP. The TUI or user-facing trigger must inject a vendor-neutral prompt containing the selected target, model, scope, required handoff structure, and exact swarm handoff CLI invocation. The agent authors the context file and runs the CLI; the CLI is the sole execution path and ships inside the swarm binary.

Swarm handoff is a supervised CLI workflow: after swarm handoff returns the child session id, the source agent must use swarm watch (event-driven), swarm peek, and swarm send in a bounded loop until needs_input, ready_for_review, or completed. Monitoring and steering belong in the injected prompt; the source stays alive and lineage links the child.
